Misam Abidi

Independent candidate for Governor, Tennessee · Open seat

Businessman (sales, banking, financial education and emerging technology)

Misam Abidi is an independent candidate for Governor of Tennessee from Nolensville in Williamson County. He filed as an independent in March 2026 and is listed on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot. He describes himself as a Pakistani-American businessman who moved to the U.S. in 1997 and has worked in retail, banking, sales and emerging technology.

Where Abidi stands

Cost of living / Taxes
Supports eliminating Tennessee's state sales tax on basic groceries. Says any revenue gap should be covered through spending discipline, efficiency, economic growth and, over time, new revenue such as a state wealth fund he has proposed.
Cost of living / Taxes
Proposes simplifying business tax filing, building on existing small-business relief, and reviewing the burden of taxing gross receipts rather than profits.
State budget / Social services
Proposes a Tennessee Dividend Fund, run on blockchain, to build long-term state financial assets. Argues this would reduce long-term tax pressure, but says uncertain future returns should not be used to promise immediate relief.
Education
Argues that every Tennessee student should graduate with at least one usable skill. Supports financial-literacy education, and says publicly funded schools should show learning gains, financial accountability and meaningful access.
Economic development / Data centers
Says he would make state business incentives transparent so taxpayers can see what their money delivers.

Background

  • Moved to the United States in 1997 (per campaign site)
